ALGER, 01/07/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Le mi: ALGIERS, 07/01/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zourouki, chaired an important video-conference coordination meeting this Wednesday with the General Secretariat of the African Telecommunications Union (ATU), in the presence of the Nigerian Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, in his capacity as President of the 7th session of the ATU Plenipotentiary Conference.
Réunion préparatoire pour le 7e Congrès: Preparatory meeting for the 7th ATU Plenipotentiary Conference
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zourouki, chaired a video-conference coordination meeting this Wednesday, July 1, 2026, organized at the initiative of the General Secretariat of the African Telecommunications Union (ATU). This meeting, held in the presence of the Nigerian Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy — appointed President of the 7th session of the ATU Plenipotentiary Conference — is part of the final preparations for this major continental event.
La 7e session du Congrès des délégués pe: The 7th session of the ATU Plenipotentiary Conference is scheduled for July 23 and 24, 2026, in Abuja, capital of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, which is hosting the event. This edition is of particular importance to Algeria, which currently holds the presidency of the current session of the Conference. Minister Zourouki reaffirmed Algeria's commitment to ensuring close coordination with the ATU General Secretariat and the Nigerian authorities to guarantee the success of this strategic event for the telecommunications sector in Africa.
Cette réunion de coordination s'inscrit: This coordination meeting is part of a drive to strengthen African cooperation in the field of telecommunications, a key sector for the continent's socio-economic development. For Algeria, which holds the presidency of the current session of the Conference, this responsibility represents a major opportunity to consolidate its role as a regional leader and promote its digital transformation initiatives, notably through projects such as the Digital Plan 2030.
La réussite de ce Congrès à Abuja permet: The success of this Conference in Abuja will also strengthen Algeria's position within African telecommunications regulatory bodies, where it already plays an active role via the Post and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE). This leadership is essential to defend the interests of Algerian operators, such as Algérie Télécom, Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo, in an increasingly competitive continental environment.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
L'Algérie compte aujourd'hui plus de 50: Algeria now has more than 50 million mobile subscribers, with a penetration rate exceeding 120% in 2025, according to the latest ARPCE data. The telecommunications sector represents a strategic pillar of the national economy, with massive investments made by Algérie Télécom, which has deployed more than 50,000 km of fiber optics and now covers 95% of the national territory with 4G. Operators Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo, operating under an ARPCE license, actively contribute to improving coverage and quality of service, despite challenges related to competition and growing user demands.
Le Plan numérique 2030, lancé par les po: The 2030 Digital Plan, launched by the public authorities, aims to accelerate the digitalization of the Algerian economy by modernizing infrastructure, developing digital skills, and fostering innovation. In this context, ARPCE plays a central role by regulating the sector and ensuring fairness among stakeholders. Public and private investments in telecommunications infrastructure, estimated at over 300 billion Algerian dinars since 2020, reflect the importance attached to this sector by the Algerian authorities.
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zourouki, emphasized: "Algeria is fully committed to supporting the preparations for this continental Congress, in coordination with the ATU General Secretariat and the Nigerian authorities. Our goal is to make this 7th session a success, both technically and politically, in order to strengthen our collaboration with African countries and promote a shared vision for the development of telecommunications in Africa."
De son côté, le ministre nigérian des Co: For his part, the Nigerian Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy reaffirmed his country's commitment to hosting an exemplary Congress, while praising Algeria's involvement in the preparations. "Algeria's presidency of the current session of the Congress is proof of the trust that Africa places in our country. Together, we must meet the challenges of the sector and seize the opportunities offered by digital transformation," he stated.
Les prochaines semaines seront consacrée: The coming weeks will be devoted to finalizing the logistical and technical details of the July 2026 Congress in Abuja. An Algerian delegation, comprising representatives from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, ARPCE, and national operators, will travel to the site to participate in the final coordination meetings. The objective is to guarantee flawless organization, both for the plenary sessions and for the thematic workshops that will be organized on the sidelines of the event.
Ce Congrès représente une étape cruciale: This Congress represents a crucial milestone for Algeria, which will be able to present its progress in terms of regulation, innovation, and connectivity. It will also offer a platform to strengthen partnerships with other African countries, particularly in the fields of cybersecurity, 5G, and the digital economy. The conclusions of this Congress will serve as a basis for the strategic guidelines of the telecommunications sector in Africa for the coming years.
